Automated Essay Scoring (AES) entails a dual challenge of evaluating both content and language. This study introduces a novel AES framework leveraging a pre-trained transformer-based language model, specifically utilizing the BERT base uncased model. The methodology involves training the model on a subset of the dataset to act as a proxy for the full data distribution, given BERT's capacity to rapidly adapt to target domains. The resulting system achieves a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.749 with human scores on the English portion of the JeDi dataset, surpassing the performance of existing state-of-the-word approaches.

Adapting object detectors to new domains often results in elevated false positive (FP) rates due to background clutter. While current mitigation strategies rely on learning box re-rankers, their effectiveness is compromised by spurious FPs in the training data. This paper introduces an unsupervised approach to adaptively adjust the adaptive regression of a domain-adapted pedestrian detector. This method eliminates the need for external re-rankers and dynamically lowers the threshold for accepting false positives without sacrificing true detection performance. Extensive experiments on the CityPersons dataset demonstrate that our approach achieves a substantial 10.8% reduction in false positives while simultaneously improving mean Average Precision (mAP) by 1.1%.

We introduce a straightforward yet potent approach to enhancing music tracks utilizing image translation and spectral gating techniques. This approach is designed to broaden the utility of deep learning-based image-to-image translation, demonstrating that these models can effectively perform audio spectral processing. Specifically, we train a deep learning architecture to convert a "raw" spectral representation of a song into an enhanced version. Empirical results indicate that the resulting audio surpasses human listening thresholds, with the method achieving an average improvement of 1.15 dB in signal-to-noise ratio. Furthermore, this methodology establishes a new benchmark for blind music denoising, achieving a significant 10 dB reduction in background noise.

This paper introduces FauxThrow, a virtual reality framework designed to investigate throwing mechanics by enabling users to execute inaccurate point-of-release releases. Through motion capture, the system gathers data on users' kinematic adjustments when deliberately aiming for erroneous release locations. The findings reveal that participants successfully correct these errors by modifying their movements upstream of the intended mistake; specifically, they adjust the point of release to a location temporally and spatially closer to the target. Furthermore, the study observes that throwing trajectories remain largely consistent across different release locations, and that arm angular velocities and linear accelerations are significantly influenced by variations in the release point. Ultimately, the paper discusses the potential applications of FauxThrow in sports training and rehabilitation contexts.

This study introduces a novel, top-down, syntax-aligned tree-structured decoding framework designed for joint neural machine translation (NMT) and parsing. The approach employs a left-to-right sequence-to-sequence architecture to generate a linearized syntax tree, effectively integrating the structural constraints of syntax-aware parsing directly into the translation process. By utilizing a dual-beam search strategy, the method simultaneously produces the translated output and the corresponding syntax tree. Experimental results demonstrate that this model achieves competitive translation performance on the WMT14 German-English benchmark, delivering high-quality syntax parsing with a 90.0% F1 score on the CoNLL shared task. Additionally, the model exhibits superior parsing efficiency, completing translations and analysis in under 0.15 seconds per sentence.

Accurate binding energies are essential for astrochemical models to simulate molecular formation on interstellar dust grains. However, existing databases often lack the necessary precision and coverage to address the specific needs of this field. To resolve this, we introduce the Binding Energy Assessment Platform (BEAP), a web-based tool that aggregates binding energy data from quantum chemical literature. BEAP enables users to access binding energies for any specified reactant pair and readily identify suitable computational methods and basis sets for their desired chemical species. Furthermore, the platform offers the capability to upload newly calculated binding energies, thereby expanding the available dataset. By BEAP, researchers can significantly expedite their work by bypassing the time-consuming process of manually reviewing and cross-referencing published binding energies.

This study examines a class of continuous-time stochastic processes characterized by a lower bound that varies with sample path. We propose a straightforward lower-bound estimation method applicable to discrete-time observations, which enables the approximation of key metrics including the expected value, variance, and the distribution of the first-passage time. We also present a technique for reconstructing process trajectories from discrete data and discuss their application in analyzing neuronal spiking activity.

We introduce a novel framework for evaluating expectation values of local Hamiltonian terms by leveraging the distribution of measurements across random circuits composed of low-depth random Clifford gates. This approach employs a "shadow" technique that reconstructs the full quantum state via a specific set of classical shadows, which are built from measurement outcomes and their corresponding quantum operations. Our analysis demonstrates that utilizing these randomized, circuit-based shadows offers a significant advantage over traditional single-qubit measurements, particularly when applied to generic, non-local Hamiltonians. Furthermore, we establish a link between circuit complexity and the depth of random circuits serving as effective shadows, showing that specific Hamiltonian classes—including those with short-range interactions and k-local Hamiltonians—can have their expectation values reconstructed with a high probability using circuits that scale polynomially with system size.

This work examines the scattering transform associated with the defocusing hydrodynamic-stability-dressed Davey-Stewartson II equations. We demonstrate that the singularities of the reflection coefficient exhibit strong dependence on the magnitude of the wavenumber, $|k|$. This finding indicates that the inviscid and hydrodynamically stable regime of these equations is highly sensitive to the initial data profile.

This paper introduces a new class of modifications to text representations, designed to enhance the robustness of pre-trained language models (PLMs) for downstream applications. We term these transformations Sibylvariant, as they adhere to the principles of the Sybil Attack framework. By utilizing a pre-trained model to generate pseudo-labels for unlabelled data, we train a second model on these generated labels. This approach offers a robust alternative to standard data augmentation techniques, which often rely on fragile pretrained models. Our analysis demonstrates that Sibylvariant methods are effective for improving performance in text classification tasks.

This work introduces a method for learning a linear representation that achieves provable guarantees for robustness and sample efficiency. We establish a non-parametric framework that is robust to adversarial noise, with the magnitude of this robustness quantified by the noise's condition number. Furthermore, we prove that learning this linear representation requires only a constant number of samples, provided the data distribution is sufficiently rich. In contrast to prior approaches that rely on computationally intractable deep representations, our method utilizes a linear representation that is both efficient to compute and learns reliably with few examples. Empirical results across multiple robust classification benchmarks confirm that this representation offers strong protection against attacks, surpassing the performance of state-of-the-art deep learning models.

Neural machine translation (NMT) models are typically trained on substantial multilingual datasets, yet many target languages possess only limited data. To address this, knowledge distillation has emerged as a strategy to leverage knowledge from models trained on larger, multilingual corpora. However, the stability of the resulting low-resource language models remains uncertain. This study evaluates the reliability of distillation and quantization techniques for low-resource languages by analyzing their performance stability. Our findings indicate that while distilled models are generally robust, those subjected to quantization exhibit instability. Specifically, we observe that quantized models trained on minimal data suffer from significant performance degradation. This study underscores the necessity of rigorous evaluation protocols for low-resource languages, advocating for the use of multiple independent language pairs to ensure model robustness.

We introduce a novel Lagrangian density for a single hypergraph, built upon an energy framework that accounts for both isolated edges and specific triangular configurations. This approach enables the derivation of equation systems governing a specific class of non-linear partial differential equations. Additionally, we propose a numerical method capable of generating a discrete approximation of the hypergraph's ground state.

Deep learning models typically demand vast amounts of labeled data for training, a challenge that is often difficult to address in medical imaging. This study investigates the efficacy of various data augmentation techniques in reducing the labeled dataset size required for pneumonia segmentation within chest X-rays. Utilizing a U-Net architecture, we trained on subsets of data ranging from 10% to 100% of the total available labeled set, applying augmentations such as random crops, flips, and erasing. Our results indicate that these augmentation strategies significantly lower the dependence on extensive labeled data without compromising model performance. Furthermore, the proposed pipeline is compatible with other architectures and can be adapted for diverse biomedical image segmentation challenges.

Although current image describing models have reached significant performance levels, they struggle to render controllable outputs. This paper introduces a prompt-based approach designed to achieve image description controllability. By utilizing a pre-trained vision-language model, we employ prompt engineering to guide the generation process. Specifically, we apply prompt-based optimization to maximize the likelihood of the model conditioned on an input image and a description prompt, thereby generating the target sentence. Furthermore, we formulate a novel objective function that jointly optimizes both the generating model and the generating process. This dual-framework approach allows for flexible control over various aspects of the final output, including specific word selection, sentence structure, and even the source image itself. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method surpasses current state-of-the-art techniques in achieving image description controllability.

This paper offers a novel characterization of harm grounded in causal theory. We define an individual as harmed by an event if they would have been in a superior state of affairs had that event not occurred. This approach diverges from traditional frameworks by eliminating the necessity for a pre-existing baseline of normality and by refracting away from reliance on moral judgments. Instead, our characterization utilizes the counterfactual difference method to identify whether damage has occurred, while incorporating the causal responsibility of the event to ensure that merely being worse off due to inaction does not automatically constitute a claim of harm.

This paper introduces MMLSpark, a comprehensive deep learning framework built on Microsoft's unified machine learning ecosystem, designed to facilitate the rapid prototyping and deployment of scalable models. By offering end-to-end support for core deep learning tasks—including data preparation, model training, and deployment—MMLSpark empowers developers to seamlessly transition from experimenting with local notebooks to scaling solutions across distributed cloud environments. The framework provides out-of-the-box implementations for numerous popular architectures, such as CNNs, RNNs, LSTMs, and Transformers, alongside flexible interfaces for custom model design. Additionally, it features specialized tools for optimizing model performance through techniques like knowledge distillation and transfer learning. The authors demonstrate the framework's versatility by applying it to various computer vision and natural language processing challenges, including image classification, object detection, semantic segmentation, text classification, and text generation.

Voice translation, which converts a speaker's utterance from one language into the same language of origin but translated, is a highly valuable technology with applications in teleconferencing, media, and more. This study introduces Zero-shot Voice Translation (ZVT), a novel approach that requires no voice examples or sentence pairs for specific target languages. ZVT is built on a unified framework that simultaneously models speech recognition, machine translation, and text-to-speech synthesis. By leveraging the interdependence of these tasks, we achieve high-quality ZVT performance. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing approaches, delivering state-of-the-art results on available datasets.

This study examines a Coleman-Gurtin model for heat transfer featuring spatially varying boundary conditions on both insulated and non-insulated segments. The analysis establishes well-posedness via a weak solution approach and demonstrates that the associated semigroup is analytic. Furthermore, the work provides the necessary conditions for asymptotic stability and characterizes the system's long-term behavior.

This study introduces a novel probabilistic load forecasting framework for low-voltage grids that merges a deep learning model with traditional statistical methods to combine day-to-day and day-ahead forecasts. The deep learning component utilizes a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) architecture to integrate historical data, generating a probability distribution of future demand. This distribution is then refined by a Bayesian model that fuses it with a day-ahead prediction derived from a linear regression of demand against historical demand and statistical regressors. The effectiveness of this fusion strategy is validated through extensive testing on real-world datasets from Germany and the UK, demonstrating a significant reduction in peak errors compared to the LSTM model alone.

This paper outlines a framework for synthesizing domain knowledge into machine learning models. It introduces a taxonomy of knowledge types and a typology of techniques for embedding such knowledge into ML algorithms. Additionally, the study presents a domain-specific framework for knowledge representation tailored to knowledge graphs, a technique that has been validated through an implementation involving the integration of biomedical domain knowledge into a neural network model.

The ongoing COVID-19 pandemic has caused widespread devastation, prompting an urgent need for effective diagnostic tools. While Chest X-ray (CxR) screening is a cost-effective and readily available method, the development of automatic algorithms for detecting COVID-19 lesions remains hindered by the scarcity of large, high-quality annotated datasets. To address this, we introduce a novel framework for the unbiased localization and segmentation of COVID-19 lesions using weakly supervised learning. This approach utilizes CXR images with only class-level labels, eliminating the requirement for labor-intensive pixel-level annotations. Our method consists of two primary stages: first, it trains a localization network to identify lesion regions by leveraging the correlation between lesion labels and image-level text descriptions. Second, it performs high-resolution segmentation within the identified areas using a self-training strategy. Extensive experiments on two prominent COVID-19 CxR datasets demonstrate that our proposed framework achieves competitive performance in both lesion classification and segmentation tasks.

Accurate localization and identification of vertebrae are critical for diagnosing spinal disorders and for training deep learning models. Although deep learning has recently advanced this field, existing methods often struggle with edge cases, such as deformed or severely degenerated vertebrae. In response, we introduce a novel deep learning framework that anatomically constrains the localization and segmentation of vertebrae within clinical CT scans. Our approach utilizes a segmentation network guided by anatomically plausible constraints to produce precise segmentation masks. These masks are then employed to generate a 3D centerline, which is further refined through a new optimization technique designed to align with the inherent geometry of the spine. Experimental results demonstrate that this method surpasses current state-of-the-art techniques, achieving a mean absolute localization error of 1.85 mm and a mean identification error of 1.16 vertebral bodies.

We investigate electron scattering from a metal surface when the region is subjected to intense laser fields, demonstrating that the combined influence of vacuum fluctuations and the laser can resonantly suppress autoionization decay. This represents a surface-level manifestation of laser-induced dynamical stabilization, an effect previously identified in atomic physics. Our analysis employs the relativistic time-dependent density matrix formalism, which accounts for the full spatiotemporal evolution of the laser-matter-vacuum interaction. We find that the stabilization mechanism is highly sensitive to the polarization and intensity of the field, as well as the specific electronic states of the scatterer. Furthermore, the effect persists even when the laser is switched off, leaving a lasting reduction in decay rates. These findings suggest that laser-controlled electron scattering could become a viable tool for probing electron dynamics in time- and space-resolved manners within the context of light-matter interactions at the attosecond scale.

This paper introduces a new approach to locomotion learning for elastic-legged robots, presenting the first open-source, high-fidelity simulation environment for quadrupeds with elastic actuators. Built upon MuJoCo, this simulator offers realistic dynamics for both robots featuring a new spring tendon architecture, which we designed to achieve more natural and stable walking patterns. To leverage these compliant legs, we developed a reinforcement learning algorithm capable of mastering locomotion in this complex setting. Our results demonstrate that the proposed method successfully learns to walk on flat terrain and navigate various hilly landscapes.

We introduce a novel approach to the problem of quantum separability by employing the concept of mutual information. This technique involves the minimization of an energy-like functional, which can be solved using the Rayleigh-Ritz variational principle. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method by applying it to the Hamiltonian of the two-qubit system described by the Bell state.

We investigate the dynamics of a novel small-scale instability that emerges in collisionless slab plasmas subjected to a uniform background magnetic field and a mean flow shear. This mode arises from the interaction between Alfv\'en waves propagating parallel to the magnetic field and the velocity shear, with the latter driving the instability. While this phenomenon shares fundamental characteristics with the well-documented kinetic Alfv\'en wave shear instability (KAWSI)—such as the formation of current sheets and the generation of particle non-thermality—it exhibits distinct differences. Specifically, the new mode operates at a shorter wavelength, with scales comparable to the Larmor radius, and operates across a broader spectrum of plasma parameters. Furthermore, it induces a specific type of particle anisotropy, increasing velocity dispersion along the magnetic field direction. These unique features suggest that the mode could significantly influence the evolution of current sheets and the development of kinetic anisotropies in astrophysical plasmas.

We introduce a novel Semi-supervised Feature-level Trait Manipulation (SFTM) framework designed to enhance fashion image retrieval. Our approach leverages the inherent traits of clothing garments to generate semi-supervised modifications, enabling the learning of more discriminative features. Specifically, semi-supervised modification involves two key steps: semi-translation and manipulation. Semi-translation entails semi-supervisedly cropping a garment segment and repositioning it onto a new background image, while manipulation refers to semi-supervisedly altering specific traits of that garment. These interventions produce semi-supervised variants of an image, establishing powerful image-image pairs that facilitate the training of a semi-supervised contrastive loss function. Semi-supervised variants are created by semi-supervisedly applying these changes to a given image. This study introduces a novel dual gradient approach for addressing ill-posed linear equations of the form $Ax = y$, where $A$ is a linear operator mapping between two real Banach spaces. We demonstrate that, provided appropriate assumptions hold, this method converges to a specific minimizer of the discrepancy principle. Furthermore, we establish convergence rates for both the primal and dual variables within the principle framework. These findings generalize and significantly expand upon existing results by Scherzer et al. (2006), which were limited to Hilbert spaces.

Light field cameras capture multi-view imagery from a single shot, enabling efficient depth estimation through multi-view stereo (MVS) algorithms. However, traditional MVS methods face significant computational hurdles, including the need to process vast numbers of views and the heavy cost of feature matching. While deep learning has emerged as a promising alternative for MVS, it typically demands extensive training data and struggles with generalization. To address these issues, we introduce a cost-building approach for constructing depth maps that leverages the structural information inherent in light field data. By explicitly modeling the structural characteristics of the cost volume, our method enhances the accuracy of cost aggregation. Furthermore, we incorporate an occlusion-aware cost builder to mitigate the impact of occluded regions. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves superior performance compared to existing techniques, particularly in complex scenes with dense occlusions.

Using a bilinear method, we derive an asymptotic solution for the foka-symmetric lensells equations, which are identified as the only pair of non-integrable equations within this specific non-integrable set.

We derive the double field theory framework for non-Riemannian metrics defined as the direct sum of a rank-2 symmetric tensor and a rank-1 vector. This construction yields a four-derivative action that reduces to Riemannian double field theory when the vector component vanishes. We demonstrate that our model corresponds to the low-energy effective theory of a non-Riemannian Rotostring, a novel extended object extending the concept of the Rotostring previously identified by Berman et al. Furthermore, we establish that a specific limit of this framework reproduces the action for a vector-spinor membrane described by a Roto-spinor membrane.

The proliferation of wireless devices in modern homes has strained the capacity of standard 802.11 networks, often resulting in poor performance. While 802.11k and 802.11v protocols offer mechanisms to enhance this performance, their adoption remains limited. This paper introduces a novel solution that leverages 802.11k to identify the optimal Access Point (AP) or extender for device connection based on current channel load. By evaluating channel utilization metrics, the proposed method directs devices toward the least congested AP or extender, thereby maximizing network efficiency.
